about.title: About Femio
about.intro: Femio is one account for a woman’s whole health life — from puberty and cycles through trying to conceive, pregnancy, postpartum, and menopause.

points.heading: Our mission
points.body: Give every woman referenced, judgment-free health knowledge and honest tracking she can trust — in her language, on her terms.

points.heading: Learning & tracking
points.body: Femio helps you understand and track your health. It is a wellness and education tool, not a medical device, and it never replaces your clinician’s care.

points.heading: Referenced, reviewed content
points.body: Every guide is sourced from reputable medical bodies and checked by a qualified clinician before it goes live.

points.heading: Honest predictions
points.body: We show ranges and a confidence level, never a single false-certain date.

points.heading: Privacy by design
points.body: Your health data is yours — never sold, never shared with advertisers. You can export or delete it anytime.

points.heading: Arabic & RTL first-class
points.body: Femio is built for English, Arabic, French, and Spanish, with right-to-left support native throughout.

editorialPolicy.title: Editorial policy
editorialPolicy.intro: Every health claim on Femio is traceable to a reputable source, every page is reviewed by a qualified clinician before it goes live, and every language is medically correct — not merely translated.

points.heading: Evidence over opinion
points.body: Every fact traces to a top-tier source such as WHO, CDC, NHS, or ACOG. We never invent statistics or guideline positions; a claim we cannot source is cut.

points.heading: At least two sources per page
points.body: Each guide cites at least two independent sources — at least one from a leading medical body — stored and shown so you can check them yourself.

points.heading: Plain language
points.body: English guides are written at about a grade 6–8 reading level; other languages target the same clarity, with any jargon defined on first use.

points.heading: Safety foregrounded
points.body: Guides include a specific when-to-see-a-doctor section, and a clear seek-care-now box wherever a symptom can be an emergency.

points.heading: Independent of advertising
points.body: Medical content is editorially independent. Advertisers never influence what we publish, and ads are never targeted using your health data.

points.heading: Kept current
points.body: Every page is re-reviewed at least every 12 months, and sooner whenever guidance changes.

medicalReview.title: How we review content
medicalReview.intro: No health content goes live on Femio until a qualified clinician has reviewed and approved it — our system refuses to publish anything unreviewed.

points.heading: Draft, review, approve, publish
points.body: An editor writes to our page standard and adds sources; a medical reviewer checks accuracy, source fidelity, and safety framing; only a reviewer can approve, and only approved content can be published.

points.heading: Qualified reviewers
points.body: Reviewers are licensed clinicians appropriate to the topic, such as OB-GYN or family medicine. Their name, credentials, and the last-reviewed date appear on every page they approve.

points.heading: Every language reviewed
points.body: A translated page cannot go live without that language’s own medical-reviewer sign-off. Good translation is never a substitute for medical review in that language.

points.heading: Enforced, not aspirational
points.body: These gates are built into our system: reviewer-only approval, approval before publishing, per-language sign-off, and 12-month re-review dates.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Your health data is yours. This page explains in plain language what Femio collects, why, who else can see it, and how you take it back or delete it.

draft.title: Draft — not yet in force
draft.body: We publish this early so you can see our intentions before you trust us with anything. Our lawyers and data-protection officer are finalising the binding version, and the company name and contact details below are still to be confirmed. Femio is not open to the public yet.

points.heading: Who we are
points.body: Femio is the controller of the data described here. The registered company, our data-protection officer and our EU representative are being appointed now; their names and contact details will appear here before launch.

points.heading: What we collect
points.body: Account basics (a pseudonymous ID, your email if you create an account, your age band, your language) and the health information you choose to enter: cycle and period dates, symptoms, mood, vitals, medicines, lab results you type in, screening-questionnaire answers, and your life stage. We also keep the minimum technical data needed to run the site securely. We do not collect anything a feature you use doesn’t need.

points.heading: Why we may hold health data
points.body: Health data gets the strongest protection in law, so we ask for your explicit consent before the first health field is stored — and we ask separately for each purpose: core tracking, pattern insights, and research (entirely optional). You can withdraw any of them at any time without losing your account.

points.heading: How our estimates work
points.body: Our estimates come from your own logs and general cycle patterns. They are shown as ranges with a confidence level because they are genuinely uncertain; they are for learning and planning, and they are not medical advice or a reliable way to avoid pregnancy.

points.heading: Who else sees it
points.body: Only the service providers we need to run Femio, each under a written data-protection contract and only for the minimum they need. Our database and hosting provider is the only one that holds health data. We never sell your data, and we never give health data to advertisers or third-party analytics tools. Any advertising we run in future will be based on the page you are reading, never on what you have logged.

points.heading: Where it lives
points.body: Femio’s database is hosted in the European Union. If a provider we use sits outside the EU, we put a lawful transfer safeguard in place first and record it in our processor register.

points.heading: How long we keep it
points.body: Your records stay while your account exists, so your history can span your whole health life — that is the point of Femio. Delete part of it, or all of it, whenever you want; deletion cascades through our systems, including backups on their normal rotation.

points.heading: Your rights
points.body: You can see your data, export a full copy as a file, correct it, delete your account entirely, withdraw a consent, or object to a use. Export and delete are buttons in the app, not a support queue, and we aim to complete any request within 72 hours.

points.heading: Anonymous mode
points.body: You can track without giving us an email at all. If you add one later, nothing you logged is lost.

points.heading: Teens and guardians
points.body: Teen mode carries no advertising, no direct messages and minimal data collection. Where a young person is below the age of consent in her country, we require a parent’s or guardian’s consent — the exact ages and the checks we use are being confirmed with lawyers in each market.

points.heading: Security
points.body: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Every database row is locked to its owner by the database itself, staff access is least-privilege, and we keep a written breach procedure with a 72-hour notification clock.

points.heading: Changes and complaints
points.body: We version this page and will tell you about meaningful changes rather than quietly editing it. You can contact our privacy team about anything here, and you always keep the right to complain to your data-protection authority.

privacy.footnote: Femio is a wellness, education and tracking service. It is not a medical device and never replaces your clinician’s care.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: The deal between you and Femio: what we promise, what we ask of you, and the limits of what a tracking and education service can do.

draft.title: Draft — not yet in force
draft.body: This is our plain-language draft, published for transparency while our lawyers finalise the binding version. It is not an agreement between us yet, and the company details, governing law and liability wording below are still to be settled.

points.heading: What Femio is — and is not
points.body: Femio gives you educational content and tools to record and understand your own health. It does not give medical advice, does not tell you what is wrong with you, and does not replace your clinician. Using it creates no clinician–patient relationship. Fertile-window estimates support conception planning and awareness only — they are not a reliable way to avoid pregnancy. If you think you are having an emergency, contact your local emergency services or go to your nearest emergency department.

points.heading: Who can use it
points.body: You need to be old enough to consent to health-data processing where you live, or to have a parent’s or guardian’s consent. Teen accounts start with a safer set-up. The exact ages per country are being confirmed with lawyers.

points.heading: Your account
points.body: Keep your sign-in details to yourself, give us accurate information, and tell us if someone else gets into your account. You are responsible for what happens under it.

points.heading: Fair use
points.body: Use Femio for your own health. Don’t scrape it, break it, resell it, overload our systems, or use it to harm anyone. We may suspend accounts that do.

points.heading: Money
points.body: Femio’s core — logging, honest estimates and the health library — is free and stays free. If we add a paid tier later it will add depth and never take basics away, and we will show the price, renewal terms and refund rules before you pay anything.

points.heading: What you post
points.body: Anything you post in a community space must be lawful and respectful, and giving medical advice to other users is not allowed. You keep ownership of your own content and give us only the permission we need to show it. We may remove content that breaks these rules.

points.heading: What we own
points.body: Femio’s software, brand and original content belong to us. Guidance we cite from medical bodies belongs to them, and is credited and linked.

points.heading: Limits
points.body: We work hard on accuracy, but Femio is provided as-is, and no health information can account for your individual situation — decisions about your health are for you and your clinician. The precise disclaimers and liability limits are being drafted by lawyers, and nothing here will remove rights that consumer law gives you.

points.heading: Ending it
points.body: You can delete your account whenever you want, from inside the app, and your data goes with it. We may limit or end access if these terms are broken, or if we have to stop offering the service.

points.heading: Law and disputes
points.body: Which country’s law applies and how disputes are handled will follow the company we register, and will be stated here before launch.

points.heading: Changes
points.body: If we change these terms in a way that matters, we will tell you and give you the chance to stop using Femio.

terms.footnote: Femio is a wellness, education and tracking service. It is not a medical device and never replaces your clinician’s care.
